New Signatures

1999
Texas Southern University · Houston

It started on campus.

Three students, one name across their chests. Negris LeBrum was founded at Texas Southern University, a historically Black university, as a Black-owned house with something to say. Almost thirty years later, it still looks right.

Mrs. Negris

It began with a love story.

Named for Amanda Metoyer — "Mrs. Negris" — a French Creole woman whose 1940s romance became the soul of the house.

Every collection carries that inheritance: the grace of Creole Louisiana, the spirit of the American frontier.

N · L
Established 1999

The House of Negris LeBrum

Negris LeBrum was born at Texas Southern University in 1999, named in honor of Amanda Metoyer — known affectionately as "Mrs. Negris." A French Creole woman from Louisiana, her 1940s love story, lived out in a divided America, became the emotional foundation of the house.

More than two decades on, that story still guides the work: luxury Western ready-to-wear designed for women who carry heritage with confidence. The tailoring nods to Creole refinement; the spirit belongs to the frontier.

Independent, intentional, and rooted in where it came from — this is Negris LeBrum America.

— Negris LeBrum
